one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 1.3x fair value. Interesting below about $185.

profile.what: JPMorgan Chase is the largest US bank, with leading positions in consumer banking (Chase), credit cards, investment banking, trading, commercial banking and asset and wealth management.
profile.money: Net interest income, the gap between what it earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors, is roughly half of revenue. The rest is fees: card interchange, investment-banking advice and underwriting, trading, and asset-management fees. Its huge low-cost deposit base keeps funding costs down.
profile.valued: Banks are valued on price to book value (or tangible book) relative to their return on equity, and on P/E. JPMorgan earns the highest premium among large US banks because its return on equity has stayed near 20% through cycles.
profile.peer_group: Financials · bank, insurer or asset manager

meaning.what_it_does: The largest US bank: consumer banking, cards, investment banking and asset management.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: The spread between loan and deposit rates, plus fees from cards, trading and advice.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: A huge low-cost deposit base and leading positions in almost every banking business.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: A severe credit cycle, or a trading or risk-control failure.

moat.summary: The lowest funding costs and broadest franchise in US banking.

valuation.method: Banks are valued on book value, not free cash flow. Justified price-to-book = (ROE − 3% growth) ÷ (required return − 3%), using a normalised ROE of 15.9% (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM, capped at 25%) and a required return of 11% (low) to 9% (high): 1.62–2.15 × book value per share of $139.99.

methods.name: Excess-return model on book value
methods.basis: Book value per share $139.99 × 1.62–2.15. This is how Damodaran values banks and insurers: equity is worth book value plus the returns earned above the cost of equity.
